after.reviewed_notes: John the Baptist was a historical first-century Jewish preacher whose public preaching is commonly placed around 29 CE. Herod Antipas later imprisoned and executed him, but the exact execution chronology is disputed: Josephus independently reports the execution without supplying a precise calendar year, and scholarship notes tension between the New Testament sequence and the chronology surrounding Antipas and Aretas. ATLAS therefore records an approximate c.29–30 CE religious-activity interval as a conventional display range, not as a claim that either boundary is exact.
